about.title: Hermosa Beach Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Hermosa Beach is a small beach town, but its main corridors — Pacific Coast Highway, Hermosa Avenue, Pier Avenue, and Manhattan Avenue — carry heavy weekend and after-work traffic, especially on Friday afternoons when reported collisions tend to cluster. Most crashes here result in injury, not tragedy, but when a fatal collision does happen, the surviving family is left to sort through grief, funeral arrangements, and unanswered questions about what happened and why. California allows a spouse, domestic partner, or children to bring a wrongful death claim, and other dependents or heirs may qualify if no immediate family survives. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free service that listens to what happened, gathers the basics, and connects your family with an independent Los Angeles County attorney who handles wrongful death matters on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to find out where you stand.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You File in California

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Can Bring the Claim
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible only if none of those survive. An attorney can confirm who in your family qualifies before anything is filed.

items.title: The Clock Starts at Two Years
items.desc: California generally gives families two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though claims against a government entity carry a much shorter deadline. Waiting too long can close the door on the claim entirely, so early guidance matters.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond the Bills
items.desc: California law allows recovery for funeral costs and lost financial support, but also for the loss of love, companionship, and guidance the family will no longer have. A civil wrongful death case proceeds separately from any criminal case tied to the same crash.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No. A criminal case is brought by the state and focuses on punishing the driver, while a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action brought by the family seeking compensation. The two can move on different timelines, and one doesn't have to finish before the other starts.

items.question: My family member died in a crash near Pier Avenue and Hermosa Avenue. Does the location matter?
items.answer: Corridors like Pier Avenue and Hermosa Avenue see steady public-record collision counts, and where a crash happened can affect which agencies were involved and what evidence exists, such as traffic camera footage or reports. An attorney can look into the specific location as part of building the claim, but it doesn't change your family's underlying right to file.

items.question: What if we're not sure which family member should file the claim?
items.answer: California law sets an order of priority, typically starting with a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children. If those relatives don't exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing, and an independent attorney can sort out who qualifies before any paperwork moves forward.
